item.title: For Dyani White Hawk, Love Is an Act of Resistance
item.description: Her exhibition "Love Language" invites viewers into the vibrant cultural legacies of Native art, and connections to land, lineage, and community.

item.title: Nan Goldin Speaks Out on Art Gallery of Ontario’s Halted Acquisition
item.description: “It’s chilling that this censorship plays out especially regarding Palestine, the great exception to free speech,” Goldin told Hyperallergic.

item.title: Nan Goldin's Battle Against Censorship
item.description: Also: Street signs against fascism, Gabrielle Goliath's lesson in resistance, and how Joan Miró fell in love with America.

item.title: Pratt Manhattan Gallery Presents “RugLife”
item.description: Sculptural carpets, woven works, and reimagined textiles by 14 contemporary artists examine housing, technology, social justice, and the environment.

item.title: Ingrid Hernández Reveals Tijuana’s Hidden Beauty
item.description: Often seen as too American to be Mexican, too Mexican to be American, the city is presented by the artist as it is, not as anyone assumes it might be.

item.title: Remembering John H. Beyer, Marian Goodman, and Chung Sang-hwa
item.description: This week, we honor an architect who mended our urban social fabric, a giant of the gallery world, and a groundbreaking Modernist.

item.title: Michelangelo and Titian’s Rivalry That May Never Have Been
item.description: William E. Wallace openly uses what he calls “informed imagination” to explore the relationship between the two masters in his new study.

item.title: Another NFT Platform Bites the Dust
item.description: Nifty Gateway, which was plagued with reports of user issues, is the latest marketplace to call it quits amid a protracted NFT slump.

item.title: Smithsonian to Return Three Looted Bronzes to Indian Government
item.description: The sculptures of Hindu gods and their followers were stolen from Tamil temples and smuggled out of India in the mid-20th century.

item.title: How Trump Is Jeopardizing the US Art Market
item.description: If entering the country suddenly requires surrendering your digital life and private information, how long before artists and collectors simply choose not to come?
